2561-robert-falconer.description: A book by George Macdonald. s of all these particulars), his hat pulled down on to his projecting eyebrows, and his shoes very dusty, as with a long journey on foot--it was a hot Sunday, he remembered that--who looked at him very strangely, and without a word pushed him aside, and went straight into his grandmother's parlour, shutting the door behind him.

arxiv-1603-07278.title: Random Tensors and Quantum Gravity This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Tensor Models, Formalism and Applications. The full collection is available at http://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/Tensor_Models.html
arxiv-1603-07278.creator: Vincent RIVASSEAU
arxiv-1603-07278.description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Vincent RIVASSEAU. We provide an informal introduction to tensor field theories and to their associated renormalization group. We focus more on the general motivations coming from quantum gravity than on the technical details. In particular we discuss how asymptotic freedom of such tensor field theories gives a concrete example of a natural “quantum relativity” postulate: physics in the deep ultraviolet regime becomes asymptotically more and more independent of any particular choice of Hilbert basis in the space of states of the universe.

arxiv-2211-09045.title: Spontaneous scale symmetry breaking at high temperature
arxiv-2211-09045.creator: Z. Lalak, and P. Michalak
arxiv-2211-09045.description: Abstract We consider a scale symmetric extension of the Standard Model Higgs scalar sector. The new sector, dilaton, is responsible for the generation of mass scales and may have geometric origin in the Weyl gravity R ~ 2 \tilde{R}^{2} term. We show how temperature as a mass scale breaks scale symmetry explicitly and through a nonvanishing thermal vev.

arxiv-2307-13198.title: Change of rotation measure during eclipse of a black widow PSR J2051 − - 0827 DSPSR ( van Straten & Bailes 2011 ) , PSRCHIVE ( Hotan et al. 2004 ) and TEMPO2 ( Hobbs et al. 2006 )
arxiv-2307-13198.creator: S.Q. Wang, J.B. Wang, D.Z. Li, J.M. Yao, R.N. Manchester, G. Hobbs, N. Wang, S. Dai, H. Xu, R. Luo, Y. Feng, W.Y. Wang, D. Li, Y.W. Yu, Z.X. Du, C.H. Niu, S.B. Zhang, C.M. Zhang
arxiv-2307-13198.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by S.Q. Wang, J.B. Wang, D.Z. Li, J.M. Yao, R.N. Manchester, G. Hobbs, N. Wang, S. Dai, H. Xu, R. Luo, Y. Feng, W.Y. Wang, D. Li, Y.W. Yu, Z.X. Du, C.H. Niu, S.B. Zhang, C.M. Zhang. Black widows are millisecond pulsars ablating their companions. The material blown from the companion blocks the radio emission, resulting in radio eclipses. The properties of the eclipse medium are poorly understood.

arxiv-2510-25571.title: Perturbation Bounds for Low-Rank Inverse Approximations under Noise
arxiv-2510-25571.creator: Phuc Tran, Nisheeth K. Vishnoi
arxiv-2510-25571.description: Abstract Low-rank pseudoinverses are widely used to approximate matrix inverses in scalable machine learning, optimization, and scientific computing. However, real-world matrices are often observed with noise, arising from sampling, sketching, and quantization. The spectral-norm robustness of low-rank inverse approximations remains poorly understood.

arxiv-2601-04953.title: Triaxial Magnetars as Sources of Fast Radio Bursts
arxiv-2601-04953.creator: J. I. Katz
arxiv-2601-04953.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by J. I. Katz. I suggest that some of the mysterious temporal properties of Fast Radio Bursts (FRB) may be explained if they are produced by dynamically triaxial magnetars. If the bursts are narrowly collimated along open field lines, then observed repeating FRB may be those in which the moment of inertia tensor is only slightly triaxial and the rotation axis, open field lines and radiation point nearly to the observer.

arxiv-2606-07182.title: Audio Imitator: Controlling Timbre and Tempo in Video2Audio Synthesis with Audio Reference
arxiv-2606-07182.creator: Jiahui, Tianrui, Chunyu, Cheng, Xijuan, Feng, Longbiao

pmc-10543462.title: Gastrodin overcomes chemoresistance via inhibiting Skp2-mediated glycolysis
pmc-10543462.creator: Li Xie, Jinzhuang Liao, Wenbin Liu, Ruirui Wang, Xiaoying Li, Wei Li, Zhongsu Zhou
pmc-10543462.description: Aerobic glycolysis, a typical phenotype in human tumors, is associated with tumor progression and chemotherapy resistance. The present study demonstrated that cisplatin-resistant oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) cells exerted a stronger glycolysis ability, which was associated with hexokinase 2 (HK2) overexpression.

pmc-10566535.title: ChatGPT Conquers the Saudi Medical Licensing Exam: Exploring the Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence in Medical Knowledge Assessment and Implications for Modern Medical Education
pmc-10566535.creator: Fahad K Aljindan, Abdullah A Al Qurashi, Ibrahim Abdullah S Albalawi, Abeer Mohammed M Alanazi, Hussam Abdulkhaliq M Aljuhani, Faisal Falah Almutairi, Omar A Aldamigh, Ibrahim R Halawani, Subhi M K. Zino Alarki
pmc-10566535.description: BackgroundThe application of artificial intelligence (AI) in education is undergoing rapid advancements, with models such as ChatGPT-4 showing potential in medical education. This study aims to evaluate the proficiency of ChatGPT-4 in answering Saudi Medical Licensing Exam (SMLE) questions.MethodologyA dataset of 220 questions across four medical disciplines was used.

pmc-10705691.title: Unveiling the Immunogenicity of Ovarian Tumors as the Crucial Catalyst for Therapeutic Success
pmc-10705691.creator: Galaxia M Rodriguez, Edward Yakubovich, Barbara C Vanderhyden, Maria Barbolina
pmc-10705691.description: Simple SummaryTumor immunogenicity is one of the main factors influencing responses to cancer therapies and long-lasting antitumoral immunity. In this review, we will cover how classic and non-classic Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) class I molecules influence tumor composition and prognosis. Moreover, we explore other components of the tumor microenvironment such as the epithelial to mesenchymal transition of ovarian cancer cells.

pmc-11535325.title: Factors affecting occupational burnout in medical staff: a path analysis based on the job demands-resources perspective
pmc-11535325.creator: Zuolin Wei, Bocheng Xia, Lingli Jiang, Huaiyi Zhu, Lingyan Li, Lin Wang, Jun Zhao, Ruoxin Fan, Peng Wang, Mingjin Huang
pmc-11535325.description: ObjectiveTo assess occupational burnout conditions and work-related factors among frontline medical staff during the COVID-19 pandemic and analyse the relationships among these factors utilizing the job demands–resources (JD-R) model as a theoretical framework.MethodsAn online survey was distributed to medical staff in one city via convenience sampling during 12/29/2022–1/10/2023.

pmc-11559086.title: The changing roles of scientific journals
pmc-11559086.creator: Arturo Casadevall, Lorraine F. Clark, Ferric C. Fang
pmc-11559086.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). After centuries of relative stability, the scientific publishing world has undergone tremendous disruption and change during the first decades of the 21st century. The causes for disruption can be traced to the information revolution, which brought such benefits as rapid publication, greater connectivity, and ready access to large databases, along with less desirable practices including image manipulation, plagiarism, and other ethical transgressions.

pmc-11713172.title: Active immunotherapy, ACI‐24.060, induces anti‐Abeta antibodies with binding profiles mirroring clinically validated monoclonal antibodies
pmc-11713172.creator: Emma Fiorini, Chiara Babolin, Rakel Carpintero, Stefania Rigotti, Stefanie Siegert, Catherine Morici, Harishini Balachandiran, Jonathan Wagg, Nicolas Fournier, Lara Herriott, Piergiorgio Donati, Saskia Delpretti, Nuno Mendonca, Andrea Pfeifer, Madiha Derouazi, Marie Kosco‐Vilbois, Marija Vukicevic
pmc-11713172.description: BackgroundThe key advantage of active immunization is the induction of sustained, polyclonal antibody responses that are readily boosted by occasional immunizations. Recent clinical trial outcomes for monoclonal antibodies lecanemab and donanemab, establish the relevance of targeting pathological Abeta for clearing amyloid plaques in Alzheimer’s disease. ACI‐24.060 is a liposomal anti‐Abeta vaccine, using Abeta 1‐15 as the immunogen.

pmc-12774419.title: The placental transcriptome serves as a mechanistic link between prenatal phthalate exposure and placental efficiency
pmc-12774419.creator: Mariana Parenti, Samantha Lapehn, James MacDonald, Theo Bammler, Adam Szpiro, Marnie Hazlehurst, Drew B Day, Ciara Thoreson, Kurunthachalam Kannan, Nicole R Bush, Kaja Z LeWinn, Qi Zhao, Sheela Sathyanarayana, Alison G Paquette
pmc-12774419.description: Prenatal exposure to phthalates, pervasive endocrine-disrupting chemicals, has been linked to child health outcomes, including prematurity and low birthweight. Placental transcriptomics data can reveal mechanisms by which environmental toxicants alter placental and fetal growth. This study aims to investigate the placental transcriptome as a mediator between prenatal maternal urinary phthalate metabolites and placental efficiency.

pmc-12974822.title: Conceptions of food healthiness among nutrition and food science undergraduates: A mixed-methods study in a Spanish university
pmc-12974822.creator: Ricard Celorio-Sardà, Mari Aguilera, Claudia Soar, Maria Clara Gómez, Oriol Comas-Basté, M. Carmen Vidal-Carou, Maria Clara de Moraes Prata Gaspar
pmc-12974822.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Understanding how future nutrition and food professionals conceptualize healthy food and eating is key to aligning university training and professional practice with public health and sustainability goals. This mixed-methods study explored how undergraduate students of Human Nutrition and Dietetics and of Food Science and Technology at a Spanish university define what makes foods healthy, and how these views differ by degree, gender, and year of study.

pmc-13061967.title: Evaluation and analysis of brittleness and acoustic emission characteristics of tight sandstone under the influence of acid-treatment
pmc-13061967.creator: Weile Geng, Shengli Guo, Gun Huang, Jun Wang
pmc-13061967.description: Acid treatment has been proven to effectively reduce reservoir fracture pressure, but the variation pattern of sandstone brittleness after acid treatment remains unclear. To effectively evaluate the characteristics of brittleness changes, uniaxial compression tests were conducted on tight sandstone subjected to acid treatment for different durations, and a brittleness index evaluation method based on radial strain response was established.

pmc-13088575.title: Implementation of centering-based antenatal group care in flanders (Belgium): experiences of women and health care providers; modalities for sustainable integration into the health care system
pmc-13088575.creator: Bianca Eerens, Astrid Van Damme, Nathalie Leister, Florence Talrich, Christine McCourt, Deborah Billings, Marsha Orgill, Matty Crone, Marlies Rijnders, Katrien Beeckman
pmc-13088575.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundIn Belgium, antenatal care is characterized by one-to-one care; with limited integration of community-based approaches. Centering-Based Group Care (CBGC), derived from the CenteringPregnancy® model, offers an alternative by combining clinical follow-up, health education, and peer support in group sessions. This study focuses on the experiences of participants and facilitators with the implementation of CBGC in three Flemish cities (Aalst, Gent, Leuven) as part of the European Union GC_1000 project.

pmc-13327465.title: Enhancing Community‐Based Nursing Decision Support: Machine Learning Models for Diabetes Risk Prediction Using Home Health Nursing Notes
pmc-13327465.creator: Doyeon LIM, Aeri KIM, Hana LEE, Kyungmi WOO
pmc-13327465.description: ObjectivesThis study aimed to identify high‐risk factors for type 2 diabetes and develop a machine learning (ML)–based diabetes prediction model using nursing notes from home health care.DesignRetrospective cohort study.SampleA total 7896 medical records from 1747 patients aged ≥ 20 years who received home health care at a university hospital in South Korea over 10 years.

pmc-13431315.title: Economic Evaluations of New Vaccine Introduction in Middle-Income Countries in the Middle East and North Africa Region: A Systematic Review
pmc-13431315.creator: Chrissy Bishop, Konstantina Politopoulou, Maria Bermudez, Federico Rodriguez-Cairoli, Motuma Abeshu, Sowmya Kadandale, Ibironke Oyatoye, Saadia Farrukh
pmc-13431315.description: Background/Objectives: Middle-income countries (MICs) in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) face financial and health system barriers when introducing new vaccines. The Gavi MICs approach has supported the introduction of pneumococcal conjugate (PCV), human papillomavirus (HPV), and rotavirus (RV) vaccines; however, economic evidence from the region remains limited.

pmc-13439913.title: Effects of school-based nutrition literacy Intervention on obesity prevention in school-age students: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13439913.creator: Srichai Posri, Arpaporn Powwattana, Sunee Lagampan, Rewadee Chongsuwat, Suparee Wisawapipat Boonmanunt, Sarunya Wongkampun
pmc-13439913.description: BackgroundObesity among school-age students is a form of malnutrition resulting from excessive body fat relative to a child’s growth. Nutrition literacy plays an important role in shaping healthy eating behaviors and promoting long-term health. Although interest in this area has increased, evidence on the effectiveness and design of school-based programs to improve nutrition literacy remains limited.

pmc-13685211.title: Investigating long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) HOTAIR expression changes in ischemic stroke patients
pmc-13685211.creator: Alia Saberi, Niloufar Nabavi, Amirreza Ghayeghran, Zivar Salehi, Yaser Moaddabi, Mohammad Ebrahim Ghaffari, Haniyeh Haghanipor, Sara Khoshdooz, Ali Bonyad
pmc-13685211.description: BackgroundIschemic stroke (IS), a leading global health problem, is caused by interrupted blood flow in the brain, often due to clotting or artery constriction. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), particularly HOX transcript antisense intergenic RNA (HOTAIR), are pivotal in stroke pathophysiology.AimThis study focused on the expression levels of HOTAIR lncRNA in ischemic stroke patients.

pmc-13688537.title: Examining the Contribution of Childhood Maltreatment to the Sex Gap in Depression: Insights from the German National Cohort (NAKO)
pmc-13688537.creator: Maja P. Völker, Aina L. Kresken, Jerome C. Foo, Josef Frank, Iris Reinhard, Johanna Klinger-König, Lea Zillich, Diana S. Ferreira de Sá, Rafael Mikolajczyk, Michael Leitzmann, Patricia Fromherz, Lilian Krist, Thomas Keil, Claudia Meinke-Franze, Steffi G. Riedel-Heller, Halina Greiser, Barbara Bohn,
pmc-13688537.description: IntroductionChildhood maltreatment is a major risk factor for depression and may contribute to sex differences in depression prevalence. We examined sex-specific associations between childhood maltreatment and depression and estimated the proportion of depression cases attributable to maltreatment subtypes.MethodsWe analyzed baseline data from 159,045 participants (49.4% female; aged 19–72) in the German National Cohort (NAKO).
